title: Quant trials jotter — small-batch experiments 2026-03-13
content:
Purpose: quick running log + actionable TODOs for the small-batch quantization experiments I ran on the 7B family. Keep this lightweight — notes to self and pointers for Maya/Omar when we sync.

Summary (high level)
- Goal: find a quant config that keeps generation quality on our in-house summarization prompts while halving the token-cost compared to float16 baseline. Focus on 4-bit GGPQ/GGML variants and nf4-like schemes.
- Machine: dev1 (A10G), container image rw-infer:dev-2026-03, serving via local Redwood Private dev stack (pinned model v1.9.2).
- Quick takeaway: gptq-4bit-nf4 (per-channel) + small KV-cache warmup retained >95% ROUGE-L on dev prompts with ~2.1x token/sec improvement vs fp16. q3_k experiments looked promising latency-wise but unstable outputs on longer summaries.

Commands I ran (notes):
- export RW_MODEL=llama-7b-v1.9.2 && rw-infer compile --model $RW_MODEL --quant gptq-4bit-nf4 --out /tmp/llama7b-gptq-nf4
- rw-infer serve --model /tmp/llama7b-gptq-nf4 --batch 8 --max-latency-ms 120 --cache-enabled true
- quick eval harness: python eval/run_prompt_eval.py --host localhost:8080 --prompts eval/summarize-news/shortset.json --metrics rouge,exact_match --n=200

Raw metrics (dev run, 200 examples):
- fp16 baseline (v1.9.2): mean latency 210ms/token, throughput 28 tok/sec, ROUGE-L 31.2
- gptq-4bit-nf4 (per-channel): mean latency 110ms/token, throughput 59 tok/sec, ROUGE-L 29.8
- ggml-q3_k (sparse pack): mean latency 95ms/token, throughput 68 tok/sec, ROUGE-L 26.4 (weird truncation on long inputs)
- q4_0-static (toy): mean latency 125ms/token, throughput 52 tok/sec, ROUGE-L 28.1

Observations and hypotheses:
- nf4-like per-channel quantization consistently preserves coherence on longer summaries vs q3_k. The hallucination rate (subjective) jumps with q3_k on prompts with longer contexts (>1024 tokens).
- The KV-cache warmup (run 2-3 short queries before measuring) improves throughput by ~8% on the 4-bit runs — probably better memory layout for cached KV blocks. Need to instrument cache hits.
- Tokenization differences matter: a few examples showed tokenization-induced truncation when using the ggml toolchain; double-check tokenizer versions between compile and eval.

Prompt sets I used (variants + quick notes):
- prompt_A_simple_summarize: "Summarize the article in 3 bullets. Keep it objective." (baseline metric)
- prompt_B_instructive_long: "You are an expert summarizer. Condense the key points and provide context in one paragraph, then 2-3 bullets." (q3_k shows missing context)
- prompt_C_kv_warmup: add two warmup Qs to prime the KV cache before the real prompt. (improves latency)
- prompt_D_rewrite: ask for 'short headline' then 'one-sentence summary' (robust across quant configs)

Examples worth saving (IDs):
- EX-042: q3_k truncated the third paragraph mid-sentence (compare tokens).
- EX-114: gptq-nf4 produced an extra invented fact about dates — need to measure factuality regressions on evaluation suite.

Immediate TODOs (prioritized):
- [ ] Add KV-cache instrumentation to the dev serving image (trace cache hit/miss per request). Assigned: Soren. ETA: 2026-03-18.
- [ ] Re-run 1k eval across the longer-context benchmark with nf4 and fp16 for statistical confidence. Assigned: Maya. ETA: 2026-03-20.
- [ ] Reconcile tokenizer versions used in compile vs eval harness; add version check to compile step. Assigned: Omar. ETA: 2026-03-15.
- [ ] Try mixed-precision (q4+fp16 key/value) in serving pipeline; track cost delta. Unassigned.

Open questions / experiments to schedule:
- Does per-channel nf4 remain stable for 13B family on A100? Hypothesis: memory layout differences might reduce KV caching improvements.
- Can we adaptively pick quantization per request based on length/latency policy in the router? Quick idea: short requests -> q3_k for latency, long -> nf4 for quality. Need perf matrix.

Notes to self (non-blocking):
- Keep a copy of the raw eval outputs in s3://redwood-dev/soren/quant-runs/2026-03-13/ (already uploaded) — path includes the seed.
- PR to rw-serving: mention that 4-bit compile logs should print tokenizer hash. Link in artifacts above.
- When we present to product next week, emphasize the cost vs quality trade-offs with concrete prompts (do not use averaged metrics only).

Meeting action items (for sync 2026-03-16):
- 10m: demo nf4-vs-fp16 outputs side-by-side (Maya)
- 5m: KV cache instrumentation plan (Soren)
- 10m: roadmap for mixed-precision trials (Omar)

Random quick ideas (brain dump):
- Short-term: auto-warmup in the router for sessions predicted to have >1k tokens; cheap and low-risk.
- Long-term: per-customer quant-recommendations based on observed prompt length distributions (could be surfaced in Redwood Optimize).

End of jotter. If anything above is unclear or you want me to re-run a slice, ping in #eng-applied-ml or add a line to ENG-1873.
